chapter_title: The Sermon at Benares and For Anne Gregory

concepts.title: Gautama Buddha's Journey to Enlightenment
concepts.definition: Siddhartha Gautama, born a prince around 563 B.C., was shielded from suffering until he saw a sick man, an aged man, a funeral procession and a begging monk, after which he left home in search of enlightenment and, after seven days, became the Buddha, the Awakened One.
concepts.key_idea: The four sights of sickness, old age, death and renunciation overturned the prince's sheltered life and set him on the path to wisdom under the peepal tree.
question_patterns: how did gautama buddha leave his princely life
what sights changed siddhartha's outlook on life

solution_steps.explain: Siddhartha was a prince kept away from the pains of the world in the palace.
A sick man, an aged man, a corpse being carried, and a monk begging for alms.
After wandering for seven days, he sat under a peepal tree and attained enlightenment, becoming the Buddha.

concepts.title: Kisa Gotami's Grief and the Mustard Seeds
concepts.definition: Kisa Gotami, whose only son had died, goes from house to house asking for medicine, and the Buddha sends her back for a handful of mustard seeds from a house where no one has ever lost a child, husband, parent or friend.
concepts.key_idea: Finding death in every house she visits, Kisa Gotami understands the nature of grief, buries her child, and returns to the Buddha as his disciple.
question_patterns: what did kisa gotami ask for after her son died
why did the buddha ask for mustard seeds from a house of no death

solution_steps.explain: Kisa Gotami carried her dead son from door to door, asking for medicine that could revive him.
The Buddha set the impossible condition of seeds from a deathless household.
Finding no house untouched by death, she understood the universal law and accepted her loss.

concepts.title: The Sermon: Death Is Inevitable
concepts.definition: In his sermon at Benares the Buddha teaches that death is common to all: mortals are like earthen vessels that must break, and lamenting brings no peace, while wisdom clears the sorrow of those who see the end of all things.
concepts.key_idea: A man who seeks peace should draw out the arrow of lamentation, complaint and grief, for only wisdom can free the heart from sorrow.
question_patterns: what does the buddha preach in his sermon at benares
why are mortals compared to earthen vessels
how can a man draw out the arrow of lamentation
what is the buddha's teaching about death and sorrow
why does grieving fail to bring back the dead
what is the difference between wisdom and sorrow in the sermon

solution_steps.explain: All living beings that are born must die; death is the certain fate of every mortal.
Like earthen vessels made by the potter, human lives end in breaking, so grieving over the inevitable is useless.
Only wisdom, the sight of life's end, can draw out the arrow of grief and give peace.

concepts.title: For Anne Gregory: Beauty Beyond Appearance
concepts.definition: In Yeats's poem For Anne Gregory, the speaker argues that only God, not young men, loves a person for herself alone, since human love attaches to yellow hair or features, and Anne insists she can change her appearance by dye or cosmetics.
concepts.key_idea: The poem's message is that inner worth, not outer appearance, deserves love, and only God loves a person for herself alone.
question_patterns: what does the poem for anne gregory say about beauty
why can only god love anne for herself alone
how does anne answer the claim about outer beauty
what do young men love in anne gregory according to the poem
compare the message of the poem with the sermon
what does changing hair colour suggest in the poem

solution_steps.explain: The poet says young men love yellow hair or physical beauty, never the person alone.
Anne claims she can dye her hair brown, black or carrot, showing outer beauty can be altered.
Only religious love, God's love, values a person for her inner self alone.
